title: observability: token-level metrics + tracing dashboard and alert tuning
author: Ariana Patel
description: Add token-level metrics and tracing sections to the inference observability dashboard; tune alert thresholds for token cost and per-token latency to reduce false positives while preserving SRE visibility. Motivation: recent incidents showed token-cost spikes for certain long-context workloads and noisy alerts due to outliers in KV-prefetch latency. This change adds new panels for token_cost_per_request and token_latency_percentiles, enriches tracing spans emitted by the serving runtime with token_count and kv_cache_hit labels, and updates alerting rules and runbook guidance. Changes include dashboard JSON updates, prometheus metric renames/aliases for backward compatibility, lightweight aggregator optimizations to avoid high-cardinality blowups, unit and integration tests for metric exposition, and docs for on-call guidance. Checklist: 1) Dashboard panels implemented and reviewed, 2) Tracing spans and labels added with sampling knobs, 3) Alert thresholds tuned and new suppression window introduced, 4) Compatibility shim for old metric names, 5) Runbook updated and linked. Impact: No breaking API changes for customers, reduced alert noise by ~70% on canary environment, and observed stable token-cost aggregation latency under load. Rollout plan: feature-flagged tracing labels rolled out to 10% then progressively to 100% with monitoring, dashboard applied to staging then prod, and alert rules deployed in a controlled change window. For details see linked Linear ENG-4512 and SUP-8123.
